Why go: a classic wooden junk and a Koh Phangan sunset

Chantara is a 25 m teak junk, the kind of boat people picture when they think of sailing in Thailand: dark teak, tall masts and a wide deck. The day cruise starts late enough for a relaxed breakfast, spends the afternoon on Koh Phangan's north coast and comes home at sunset, so you see the Gulf in its best light.

What you'll do

After pickup you board at Bang Rak and have a Thai buffet lunch on the way north. The first stop is Koh Ma, where a sandbar links a small island to Koh Phangan and the reef is good for beginners. In the afternoon you have time ashore at Thong Nai Pan, one of Phangan's best beaches, before sailing back to Samui with snacks as the sun sets.

Who it suits

  • Families: under-6s sail free and there is plenty of deck space.
  • Couples and friends who want a long, social day with a sunset finish.
  • Anyone visiting in November or early December, when Ang Thong is closed.

Who should choose something else

  • Groups who want their own boat: see Chantara private charter.
  • Early risers who want limestone cliffs and lagoons: the Ang Thong big boat tour (from 16 December).

Good to know

  • Timing: the pickup is at 10:00 and you are back after dark, so plan a late dinner.
  • Drinks: alcohol isn't included; buy on board or pay corkage for your own.
  • Sea: the crossing can be rough from October to December; the captain decides on the route.

Before you book

Choose a Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday, and tell us your hotel so we can confirm the pickup time and whether the south Samui surcharge applies. Bring your own drinks if you like, but remember the corkage fee per bottle and per can.
